title: PdpBarChart top-padding is wrong-signed for all-negative categorical PDPs, pushing the zero baseline outside the plot
description: In PdpBarChart the y-axis top is computed as yMax = max(avg_prediction) * 1.1 and the bottom as yMin = Math.min(0, min(avg_prediction)). The *1.1 headroom only enlarges the visible range when the maximum is positive. When every categorical bar value is negative (e.g. a GLM / regression target whose predictions can go below zero — the codebase supports GLM models, see glm_coefficients/glm_relativities on TrainResult), max(avg_prediction) is negative, so yMax = negativeMax * 1.1 moves the top FURTHER from zero (more negative) instead of adding headroom. Then yMin = min(0, allNegative) = the most-negative value, and the computed zeroY = yScale(0) falls ABOVE marginTop (outside the plotting area). All bars are anchored at zeroY (barY = zeroY for negative values) and extend downward from a point above the chart, so they render partially outside the intended plot rectangle and the y grid/labels span an entirely-below-zero range. The bar-height geometry itself is self-consistent (verified: for v<0, zeroY + |v|/ySpan*chartH == yScale(v)), so this is purely a degraded/clipped visual layout, not a crash.
evidence: yVals = grid.map(p => p.avg_prediction); yMin = Math.min(0, yVals.reduce(min, Infinity)); yMax = yVals.reduce(max, -Infinity) * 1.1; ySpan = yMax - yMin || 1; zeroY = yScale(0) = marginTop + chartH - ((0 - yMin)/ySpan)*chartH. Example preds=[-5,-2]: yMin=min(0,-5)=-5, yMax=-2*1.1=-2.2, ySpan=2.8, zeroY = marginTop + chartH - (5/2.8)*chartH = marginTop - 0.786*chartH (above the top edge). Bars then start above the plot. The sibling numeric PdpLineChart pads symmetrically (yPad = (yMax-yMin)*0.1) and has no such issue.
